title.value: The generalizability of pre-processing techniques on the accuracy and fairness of data-driven building models: A case study
title.justification: The title clearly indicates the focus of the paper on pre-processing techniques and their impact on data-driven building models.
title.quote: The generalizability of pre-processing techniques on the accuracy and fairness of data-driven building models: A case study

extractions.description: The paper explores the impact of various pre-processing techniques on the accuracy and fairness of data-driven building models. It evaluates five pre-processing techniques, including a proposed Sequentially Balanced Sampling (SBS), using 4960 cases to predict lighting status in apartments. The study examines the trade-offs between improving predictive accuracy for minority classes and decreasing accuracy for majority classes while also considering fairness improvements in predictive models.

climate_change_is_central.justification: The paper addresses the efficiency and effectiveness of data-driven models in building management, which directly relates to energy consumption and efficiency—an important aspect of Climate Change Mitigation.
climate_change_is_central.quote: DDBMs could be used to predict indoor air temperature, energy consumption, thermal comfort, occupancy status/numbers, indoor air quality, fire hazard or HVAC system performance.
